findings.problem: The two private lemmas repeat the same argument. For a unit `d`, `v(d) ≠ 0`, so `v(d) ≤ v(T - b)` forces `v(T - b) ≠ 0`. Each proof builds `hd₀` from `(hd.map C).map v.1.valuation`. Each then rewrites `vle` into valuation inequalities and closes the goal by the same `h₀ ▸ h` / `le_zero_iff` step. The only difference is the surrounding unfolding of `mem_basicOpen_iff` versus `mem_rationalSubset_iff`. Any change to this core step, for example to the valuation API, has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private lemma, stated for `v : closedPolydisc 1 K`, `b : K` and `hd : IsUnit d`: `v.1.toValuativeRel.vle (C d) (T - C b) → ¬ v.1.toValuativeRel.vle (T - C b) 0`. The proof gets `hd₀ : v.1.valuation (C d) ≠ 0` from `((hd.map C).map v.1.valuation).ne_zero`. It then rewrites with `← valuation_le_iff`, `map_zero` and `le_zero_iff`, and finishes with `fun h h₀ ↦ hd₀ (le_zero_iff.mp (h₀ ▸ h))`. Call it `not_vle_zero_of_vle_isUnit`. Both set lemmas then reduce, after `ext v` and the existing `simp only`/`rw` unfolding, to `iff_self_and.mpr (fun h ↦ not_vle_zero_of_vle_isUnit v b hd h)`. This is stated under the same `[CommRing K] [TopologicalSpace K] [NonarchimedeanRing K]` hypotheses, so no new imports are needed. The `hd₀` lines and the closing `rw`/`exact` disappear from both proofs.
findings.benefit: The mathematical fact that a unit hole parameter forces `v(T - b) ≠ 0` is stated and proved once, with a name. The basicOpen and rationalSubset lemmas then differ only in unfolding their respective definitions, which makes that difference easier to see and keeps the two lemmas from drifting apart.
